nuevos.titulo_original: Why Your Muscles Are Getting Weaker (It’s Not Just Age)
nuevos.descripcion:
Fat infiltration in skeletal muscle is a major driver of age-related strength loss. 

Everyone can safely store only a certain amount of fat. Any fat beyond that amount is directed to your liver, your pancreas and your muscles.

For me, fat inside muscle is especially important.

Two people with the same muscle size can still have very different levels of strength. In older adults, high and increasing fat in the thigh muscle also predicted faster declines in walking speed.

In older adults with obesity who were dieting, combined cardio and strength training reduced fat between muscles by about 41%. Cardio alone reduced it by about 28%, strength alone by about 23%.

Where your body stores fat and how well your muscle handles it tell you more about your metabolic health than the number on the scale.

También te mostramos cómo tomar bien la muestra de orina y cuándo alcanza con un solo frasquito en vez de andar juntando las 24 horas. Si te toca hacerte un laboratorio, leé el papelito de las indicaciones, preguntá lo que no entiendas y contale a tu médico qué medicamentos o suplementos tomás. Un buen diagnóstico empieza mucho antes de que te saquen sangre.

Does NAD Really Drop as We Age?
nuevos.descripcion:
One of the main reasons people take NAD supplements like nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is the idea that NAD, a molecule central to our metabolism, runs low as we get older.

In a 2022 study, researchers took muscle biopsies from younger and older adults. Older adults who didn't exercise had less NAD in their muscles. Older adults who did exercise had roughly the same amount as the younger people. The lowest levels were in older adults who struggled on basic physical tests.

A 2026 study measured NAD in the blood carefully, across seven separate groups of people. Blood NAD stayed remarkably stable with age.

Some small studies do find lower NAD in older skin and brain tissue. But the idea that we all run low on NAD as we age, and need to top it back up, isn't well supported in humans.

outliers.titulo_original: ENTRAINMENT GOVERNS YOUR ENERGY & FOCUS
outliers.descripcion:
Entrainment is one of the most powerful aspects of our biology.

Our circadian rhythm is created within us, but numerous studies show that our health is best when it is entrained to the rising and setting of the sun. That’s not to say you have to wake up at sunrise, but people who try to live nocturnally definitely suffer health consequences and people who match their sleep rhythm even somewhat to the rising and setting of the sun (one form of entrainment), derive many health benefits.

Entrainment works on shorter time scales too. Exercise at roughly the same time for a few days and you’ll notice your energy will increases a few minutes before that typical workout time.

Study or do some reading or some other form of work or learning at roughly the same time or times per day, and you’ll notice that your mental sharpness will start to increase in anticipation of those times.

To be clear, some of this is psychological, but a lot of it is physiological. The neuromodulators, hormones and neurotransmitters that regulate alertness and focus are readily susceptible to entrainment.

And entrainment is a concept that we can leverage. Not to make us rigid, but understanding it can help you make better sense of why you are more energetic and mentally sharp at particular times of day, and it can give you flexibility over what those times are.
